SEARCH
Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system

Class SecurityService

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.SecurityService
public final class SecurityService extends Object
Host-security front-end for the LFS/BLFS security manager, normative in system-management-contract.md §4.6. It detects which firewall / mandatory-access-control / secure-shell backends are installed, builds the exact nft / apparmor_status / getenforce / sshd argument vectors and parses their read-only output; it never re-implements firewall or MAC logic and never writes /etc directly (mutations go through the owning CLI, §6).

Operation classes drive the UI's confirmation level:

  • SecurityService.Operation.NFT_LIST, SecurityService.Operation.APPARMOR_STATUS, SecurityService.Operation.SELINUX_MODE, SecurityService.Operation.SELINUX_ENABLED, SecurityService.Operation.SSHD_STATUS and SecurityService.Operation.SSHD_CONFIG_TEST are read-only and run unprivileged via ProcessRunner;
  • SecurityService.Operation.NFT_APPLY, SecurityService.Operation.SSHD_START and SecurityService.Operation.SSHD_STOP are mutating - confirmed, then escalated via PrivilegedRunner (polkit).
The sshd lifecycle is delegated to InitSystemService (§4.1) with sshd as the service name, so no init logic is duplicated here.

The detection, command-building and output parsing are pure and unit-testable (apparmorTool(Probes), buildCommand(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.SecurityService.Operation, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.SecurityService.AppArmorTool, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.InitSystemService.InitSystem), parse*, summarize*); the live probe() and the run* helpers are thin wrappers that degrade gracefully - an absent tool or an unsupported operation yields an empty vector / a not-started result rather than throwing.

    • buildCommand

      public static List<String> buildCommand(SecurityService.Operation op, SecurityService.AppArmorTool aaTool, InitSystemService.InitSystem init)
      Builds the argument vector for op, resolving the AppArmor tool and init system from aaTool / init. Returns an empty list when the operation is unsupported, the tool is absent, or the init system is unknown; the result never contains shell metacharacters and is meant to be handed straight to ProcessRunner / PrivilegedRunner.
      Parameters:
      op - the operation
      aaTool - the resolved AppArmor tool (only used by SecurityService.Operation.APPARMOR_STATUS)
      init - the detected init system (only used by the sshd lifecycle ops)

    • sshdCommand

      public static List<String> sshdCommand(SecurityService.Operation op, InitSystemService.InitSystem init)
      Builds the sshd vector. SecurityService.Operation.SSHD_CONFIG_TEST is the bare sshd -t; the status/start/stop operations delegate to InitSystemService.buildCommand(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.InitSystemService.InitSystem, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.InitSystemService.Operation, java.lang.String) with "sshd" as the service name (§4.1), so an unknown init yields an empty vector.

    • parseSelinuxMode

      public static SecurityService.SelinuxMode parseSelinuxMode(String output)
      Parses getenforce output into a SecurityService.SelinuxMode. Blank or unrecognised text yields SecurityService.SelinuxMode.UNKNOWN; an absent tool is reported by the caller (never a silent "secure").

    • parseSelinuxEnabled

      public static boolean parseSelinuxEnabled(int exitCode)
      Interprets the selinuxenabled exit code: 0 means SELinux is enabled, any non-zero means it is not (or is absent).

    • parseAppArmor

      public static SecurityService.AppArmorStatus parseAppArmor(String output)
      Parses apparmor_status / aa-status output. Detects whether the module is loaded and counts the processes in enforce / complain mode from the "N processes are in <mode> mode" lines. Pure and lenient: blank output yields a not-loaded, zero-count status.

    • summarizeNft

      public static SecurityService.NftSummary summarizeNft(String output)
      Summarises an nft list ruleset dump by counting the table and chain declaration lines. The full ruleset text is shown verbatim by the UI; this is only the one-line summary. Pure and lenient.

    • parseSshdState

      public static SecurityService.SshdState parseSshdState(int exitCode, String output)
      Parses an init-system status sshd result into a SecurityService.SshdState. Recognises the systemd (active (running) / inactive (dead)), runit (run: / down:) and openrc (status: started / status: stopped) shapes; negative phrases are matched first so "not running" never reads as running. With no usable text the exit code decides (0 = running for a status command).

    • isSshdConfigOk

      Interprets the sshd -t config test exit code: 0 = valid config.

    • runRead

      public static ProcessRunner.Result runRead(SecurityService.Operation op)
      Runs a read-only operation unprivileged through ProcessRunner, resolving the AppArmor tool and init system live. Returns a not-started ProcessRunner.Result when the operation is mutating, unsupported, or its tool is absent.

    • runMutating

      public static PrivilegedRunner.PrivilegedResult runMutating(SecurityService.Operation op)
      Runs a mutating operation with polkit escalation through PrivilegedRunner. The sshd lifecycle delegates to InitSystemService.runMutating(org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.InitSystemService.InitSystem, org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.system.InitSystemService.Operation, java.lang.String) (§4.1). Returns an ERROR result when the operation is read-only, unsupported, or its tool is absent. The caller MUST have confirmed first.
